text: Human Rights Watch's July 2023 investigation found that the land acquisition for TotalEnergies' Tilenga and EACOP oil projects in Uganda (operated by its wholly-owned subsidiary TotalEnergies EP Uganda) devastated the livelihoods of displaced families through multi-year payment delays and compensation below replacement cost; a 2025 University of Sheffield and Haki Defenders Foundation study of 100 affected people found compensation was still unfair and inadequate.
short: HRW (2023): TotalEnergies' Uganda oil projects' land acquisition devastated displaced families' livelihoods.

source.name: Human Rights Watch: "Our Trust is Broken" – Loss of Land and Livelihoods for Oil Development in Uganda
source.quote: this report documents the devastating impacts on livelihoods of Ugandan families from the land acquisition process.

additionalSources.name: The Guardian: "People displaced by Uganda oil pipeline 'received inadequate compensation'"
additionalSources.quote: many people reported unfair and inadequate compensation and a lack of transparency
additionalSources.note: Reports a 2025 study by Haki Defenders Foundation and the University of Sheffield based on interviews with 100 people affected by the EACOP project, a partnership including TotalEnergies.
